title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has responded to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards by outlining a set of policy measures aimed at ensuring AI is used responsibly and transparently. It commits to developing guidelines, strengthening regulatory frameworks, and fostering innovation while protecting public interests.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is setting out rules to make sure artificial intelligence is used fairly and transparently in the UK qualifications sector, so that exams and assessments remain reliable and free from bias. The policy will guide how AI tools can be tested, approved and monitored, with a focus on protecting students’ data, upholding assessment integrity and ensuring that any AI‑powered changes meet strict quality and security standards.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how artificial intelligence systems use copyrighted material, identifying both potential benefits and risks associated with this practice. It offers recommendations to balance innovation with the protection of creators’ rights and suggests policy measures to address copyright challenges in AI development.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government has issued a response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” outlining its view on the findings and recommendations. It highlights the importance of AI for the UK, pledging to take action on key issues raised by the committee.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document sets out the scope, roles, and responsibilities of a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence should meet public standards, and it includes frequently asked questions to guide its work. It clarifies the committee's objectives, the key areas to evaluate, and how it will engage stakeholders and produce recommendations.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence, offering its perspective on AI governance. The submission highlights key considerations and recommendations for policymakers to shape responsible AI policies.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The document explains how artificial intelligence is reshaping rules for medical products, focusing on safety, efficacy, and compliance. It details how the principles from the AI White Paper will be used to guide regulators in assessing and approving AI-driven medical technologies.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make our organisation the world's most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI‑driven defence force for its size. It outlines a vision for leading AI adoption, enhancing operational capabilities, and setting high standards of trust and influence within the defence community.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to unlock AI’s benefits while controlling its risks. It sets out a strategy for responsible AI use that supports innovation, safety and public trust in transport systems.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report reviews how AI systems use copyrighted material and the legal implications under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act, summarizing progress and challenges. It outlines current practices, policy updates, and recommendations for balancing copyright protection with AI innovation.
